newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy warns travelers of dangers in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Italy warns travelers of dangers in Kenya.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Ministry warned travelers to Kenya on Monday to stay clear of the Indian Ocean port city of Mombasa, which has been hit by a wave of violence in the last week.
A ministry statement also urged visitors to the Kenyan capital of Nairobi to avoid the city centre and areas close to the university "which have been the stage for violent protests."
The road from Mombasa to Malindi, about 100 km (60 miles) north on the coast, is also at risk, the ministry said.
Some 33 people have been killed since Wednesday in violence along the Kenyan coast. The latest attack happened overnight, when attackers slashed two Kenyans with machetes on the edge of Mombasa.
The Italian embassy in Nairobi said some 200 Italians were currently in Mombasa which, with Malindi, is popular with tourists relaxing on the beach after going on Safaris in the Kenyan inland.
No tourists have been hurt in the violence but thousands have been told to stay in beach hotels.
